title: Laredo Advances Water Infrastructure and City Services as 2027 Approaches, City Manager Says
excerpt: Laredo is closing 2026 with major work underway on its water system and city services, and more to come in 2027, according to a year-end statement from City Man
content:
Laredo is closing 2026 with major work underway on its water system and city services, and more to come in 2027, according to a year-end statement from City Manager Joseph W. Neeb titled "City Vision in Focus — The Work of a City Continues."

The city's top water priority is replacing aging waterlines, improving pressure management, and strengthening the water distribution system. That work has caused street closures, traffic changes, and occasional service interruptions — and Neeb said communication must be part of the project itself, not something addressed only after construction begins or problems arise. During 2026 the city expanded construction advisories, bilingual utility updates, service notifications, weather alerts, and newsletters.

Other 2026 work included investments in streets, drainage, transportation, and public facilities. The Buena Vista Sports Complex opened, and the city continued operating the international bridge system. Public safety — police, fire, EMS, and emergency management — was noted as a major responsibility.

The City Council adopted the fiscal year 2026-27 budget: approximately $1.019 billion in consolidated expenditures and a General Fund of roughly $300 million.

Looking to 2027, Neeb said he would present the mayor and City Council with a preliminary inventory of continuing priorities, and council members were invited to identify district needs and citywide goals. Some initiatives need further planning or Council consideration; others are already authorized.

"Looking back, I believe 2026 was a great year for Laredo," Neeb said, while acknowledging that not every challenge was resolved or project completed. He closed by recognizing municipal employees, including emergency responders and utility workers, working through the holidays.

Source: Texas Border Business, Nov. 23, 2026.
